item.title: The Cold War British Spy Mission the Soviets Had to Tolerate
item.author: Imperial War Museums
item.content:encoded:
Former BRIXMIS intelligence officer Peter Williams shares his first-hand experiences operating behind the Iron Curtain during the Cold War. From gathering military intelligence in East Germany to violent encounters with Soviet forces and the Stasi, Peter recounts the realities of one of Britain's most unique and dangerous military missions.

The world came frighteningly close to the greatest nuclear disaster in history, but the story of the event isn't that well known. Two hydrogen bombs ~250 times more powerful than the ones dropped on Hiroshima accidently fell on North Carolina. Both weapons hit the ground one of them very well should have gone off but didn't. Why? In this episode we explore the 1961 goldsboro b-52 incident.

item.title: The Universe Has Been Expanding Since the Big Bang. Just Not How We Thought.
item.author: PBS Space Time
item.content:encoded:
Check out the Space Time Merch Store https://www.pbsspacetime.com/shop
Last year, the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument—DESI—made headlines around the world. Its enormous map of the Universe hinted that dark energy—the mysterious something causing the expansion of the Universe to accelerate—might not actually be constant. Last month, another giant cosmology experiment released its final results. The Dark Energy Survey. DES. Its results are intriguing. But did they confirm the DESI measurement? We’ll, let’s see, but there’s also a much more interesting question—Why are completely different scientific studies so much more powerful in combination than any one study on its own? The answer brings us to the heart of what science really is.

item.title: We Didn't Predict the Sun Would Do This
item.author: Astrum
item.content:encoded:
Why was the Sun’s recent solar maximum twice as strong as predicted? In 2024-2025, the Sun entered a fiery active phase that completely defied expectations. But thanks to NASA's Parker Solar Probe, we now have observations taken from inside the Sun's atmosphere, which could help explain what’s powering the unusual eruptions. What’s really going on inside our star? And should we be worried here on Earth?
